content: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Toggl: Senior Full Stack Anywhere in the World Alabama Full-Stack Programming Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0074/7274/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Tallinn, Estonia <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://toggl.com/jobs/">https://toggl.com/jobs/</a> </p> <div class="_descriptionText_5yu8i_201 ashby-job-posting-description"> <p>We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.</p> <p>You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.</p> <p>The salary for this position is&nbsp;<strong>€83,000 annually.</strong></p> <p>You can work from anywhere in the world&nbsp;<strong>as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4.</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>The Role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.</p> <p>You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.</p> <p>Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.</p> <p>Your main responsibilities will be:</p> <p><strong>Ownership and delivery</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.</p> </li> <li> <p>Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Craft and quality across the stack</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.</p> </li> <li> <p>Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.</p> </li> <li> <p>Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Working with product and design</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.</p> </li> <li> <p>Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Raising the bar</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.</p> </li> <li> <p>Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>AI as core leverage</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.</p> </li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>About You</strong></h2> <p>You will thrive in this role if you:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.</p> </li> <li> <p>Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.</p> </li> <li> <p>Have deep, practical knowledge of&nbsp;<strong>JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS</strong>&nbsp;- including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.</p> </li> <li> <p>Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does.&nbsp;<strong>Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast.</strong></p> </li> <li> <p>Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.</p> </li> <li> <p>Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.</p> </li> <li> <p>Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket.
